hook.say: What if AI took your job... and then everyone else's?

lines.goal: Let's fast-forward until the very last job is gone. The ending might surprise you.
lines.screens: First to go: anything done on a screen. Call centers. Data entry. Translators.
lines.quiet: Nobody makes an announcement. Companies just stop hiring... and young people feel it first.
lines.safe: Then it climbs the building. Coders. Lawyers. Accountants. People who were sure they were safe.
lines.robots: Plumbers and nurses feel fine... until robots get cheap. Trucks drive themselves. Warehouses go dark, because robots don't need the lights on.

hundred.say: And then, one morning... nobody goes to work. Ever again.

lines.twist: Sounds like paradise, right? Here's the problem. No jobs means no paychecks... so who's buying anything?
lines.fix: So countries try something wild: tax the robots, and send everyone a check.
lines.finland: Finland actually tested free money. About six hundred dollars a month, no strings attached. People didn't get lazy... they got happier.
lines.history: And history has a twist. In 1900, nearly four in ten Americans farmed. Today? About one in a hundred. We didn't run out of work... we invented new kinds.

outro.say: So the real question isn't whether AI takes the jobs... it's who owns the AI.

cta.say: Which job do you think goes last?
